normalized.description: Objectives:To develop a new generation of compact and low-cost sensors and measurements techniques for health monitoring systems applied to hydrodynamics technologies, reusable and advanced propulsion systemsDescription:In the context of new missions requiring longer lifetime, increased safety and reliability for critical technologies, and in the frame of reducing the turnaround time and maintenance cost of reusable propulsion systems, a new generation of measurements techniques in combination to heath monitoring are essential. Revisions of these sensors are required to provide the necessary data to monitor the correct operational behaviour, in particular for hydrodynamics sensitive components and propulsion systems while forecasting errors, malfunctions and problems. Compared to the need in the applications, the background on sensors and measurements techniques is today at very low TRL.The present activity will start from the following hardware: Flow Rate Measurement sensor, 3D Particle Tracking Velocimetry sensor, Particle DensityMeasurement sensor, Propulsion Health Monitoring sensor, Scanning Light Sheet sensor, Particle Image Velocimetry sensor, and Optical Emission Spectroscopy instrument. Other sensors could be considered as well where relevant. This activity targets improvement of data rate capabilities, increase of sensing functions, miniaturization, and decrease of hardware cost.The activity targets also a better diagnosis during operation on ground and in flight of propulsion and flight vehicle systems. In turn advanced sensors and instruments for health monitoring systems will lead to a higher reliability for those system and faster error assessment.This activity encompasses the following tasks:- State of the art review (including spin in of COTS elements from other sectors) and gap analysis to identify potential modifications/improvements of the current sensors and health monitoring systems and benefits versus implementation cost (and time).- Trade-off of new sensors and sensing techniques and selection of most promising solution considering safety,lifetime, and cost improvement.- Design and prototype manufacturing. Selection of the set of the most important and relevant sensors and health monitoring techniques for prototype development. The developed prototype shall be able to reach the level of breadboard without flying qualified components.- Testing in functional representative environment. A subset of the developed prototypes willbe tested to verify the correct functionality and confirm the achievable level of improvement.- Conclusions, recommendations, and follow up, including a development roadmap for a complete technology maturation at higher TRL level.
